wave_title: Fifteenth generation this cycle. A real, silent data-loss defect reachable via ordinary, legal-looking ADL syntax (no grammar rule forbids a single-line block), affecting entity/capability/binding/constraint/invariant/materialize declarations alike, with zero diagnostic anywhere -- and in the materialize case, capable of flipping a real check/systemize pass/fail outcome (MISSING_MATERIALIZATION -> ATLAS-E040 -> CODING_ADMISSION_NOT_ALLOWED) based on a parser artifact rather than the actual repository state.
gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly instructed to build its own exclusion list from git log rather than a possibly-stale prior list, after several honest negative results this cycle. Its finding was independently re-verified before any change: read collect_block's real, current code directly, traced the exact iteration for a single-line block by hand (index==start, depth reaches 0 on the same iteration, `if index > start` never fires, loop breaks with an empty body), confirmed all six real call sites (entity, capability, binding, constraint/invariant, materialize -- transform discards its body intentionally via `let (_, next)`), and independently confirmed the materialize consequence chain (path defaults to "" via unwrap_or_default(), feeding a real downstream MISSING_MATERIALIZATION check) by reading that code path directly rather than trusting the subagent's description of the consequence.
key_finding: collect_block's loop unconditionally skipped pushing lines[index] into body whenever index == start (the header line), on the reasoning that a normal multi-line block's header line (`entity Foo Bar {`) carries no attribute content of its own. That reasoning is false for a single-line block, where the SAME header line also carries the closing brace and every attribute: for `capability Foo { input = A }`, the one and only loop iteration has index == start, so nothing is ever pushed to body, and the loop's own depth-reaches-zero check (satisfied on that same iteration, since both `{` and `}` appear on it) breaks immediately -- body comes back completely empty. parse_assignments(&[]) then returns an empty map, silently producing a CapabilityDecl/EntityDecl/MaterializationDecl/etc. with every attribute missing, with zero diagnostic anywhere. Verified this is not a narrow one-declaration-kind issue: all six call sites (adl/mod.rs's entity/capability/binding/constraint-invariant/materialize match arms, everything using collect_block's non-discarded body) share the identical bug, since the defect lives in the shared collect_block function itself, not in any per-declaration-kind logic.

Grepped every collect_block call site in adl/mod.rs directly (six total) to confirm the bug's real breadth across declaration kinds, rather than trusting the survey's own enumeration.

Read the materialize declaration's real downstream consequence chain (path: attrs.get("path").cloned().unwrap_or_default()) directly to independently confirm the claimed MISSING_MATERIALIZATION consequence is real, not speculative.

Confirmed via git log -S"collect_block" (already run by the survey, independently spot-checked) that this function predates this session's own prior two ADL fixes and was untouched by either -- a genuinely separate, previously-unfixed defect in the same file, not a re-discovery of already-fixed territory.

design_decisions.question: How to recover a single-line block's inline content without redesigning parse_assignments (which expects one key=value assignment per body line)?
design_decisions.decision: Extract the text between the header line's first `{` and last `}` (or end of line, if the block's closing brace is on a later line -- correctly handling a hybrid shape too, e.g. `entity Foo Bar { kind = backend` continuing on subsequent lines), then split that inline text into individual `key = value` lines via a new quote-aware tokenizer (split_inline_assignments/quote_aware_tokens) that recovers each (key, "=", value) token triple as its own synthetic body line. This matches parse_assignments' own existing one-assignment-per-line expectation exactly, rather than changing that function's contract -- both split_inline_assignments and parse_assignments now agree on the same per-line shape, just fed from a different source (a tokenized single line vs. real separate lines).

design_decisions.question: Handle only the single-attribute case (capability Foo { input = A }), or also multiple attributes crammed onto one line (materialize Compiler { path = "core" language = rust })?
design_decisions.decision: Both, via the same general tokenizer: every attribute value in this DSL is exactly one whitespace-delimited token (a bareword identifier or a "..."-quoted string), so repeatedly consuming (key, =, value) token triples correctly recovers an arbitrary number of assignments crammed onto one line, not just a single one. This was necessary to fully close the gap the survey's own materialize example demonstrated, not merely the simpler capability example.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: collect_block no longer silently discards a single-line block's own content; both a single-attribute one-liner (capability Foo { input = A }) and a multi-attribute one-liner (materialize Compiler { path = "core" language = rust }) now correctly produce every attribute, with the existing multi-line block parsing path (the style this repository's own real .atlas/declared/*.adl files use) completely unaffected.
